The clamp column here applies a per-contact tolerance rather than a flat 4 Å cut-off, so it reads higher than the clamp integrity figures in Table 1 and Figure 18; both numbers are given and neither is adjusted to the other. The two RMSD columns are the gate's own summary statistics and differ by a tenth of an ångström or so from the trajectory means in Table 1. BoPEP4_G08_alanine-scan.jpg: **Figure 22 | Alanine scan of BoPEP4 against PEPR1.** Change in HADDOCK score relative to wild type for eighteen single-point alanine substitutions, Ser6 to Asn23, each built on the validated complex with the backbone held fixed and refined identically; positive values are destabilising. Bars are coloured as binding hotspots, structural or conformational signals, and neutral positions, with the ensemble mean marked on each. Eight positions clear +7, every one of them carried by a large electrostatic term. The scan returns −1.3 and −2.9 at S15A and G17A, the two substitutions published to cost roughly 100-fold and more than 4,000-fold in activity, which bounds what the method can be asked.
BoPEP4_T04_truncation-ladder.jpg: **Table 4 | The truncation ladder in full, both receptors.** All seventeen rungs with HADDOCK score, buried surface area, AlphaFold3 ipTM and interface PAE against PEPR1 and PEPR2, and the verdict assigned to each. BoPEP4_G16_acceptance-gate-vs-atoms.jpg: **Figure 30 | The same construct under the project's gate and under an atom-resolved criterion.** Six measures of one pair of trajectories. Under the three atom-resolved measures every one reads 0.0% against 99.8 to 100% for wild type. The figure is kept because it records a gate that passed a construct it should have failed.
BoPEP4_F02_complex-wt-surface.jpg: **Figure 2 | The binding groove, coloured by side-chain class.** Solvent-excluded surface of the 316 receptor residues lining the peptide-binding groove, computed with a 1.4 Å probe and coloured basic (blue), acidic (red), polar (teal) and apolar (grey). The groove is acidic along the stretch the peptide's lysines and arginines occupy, which is the electrostatic complementarity the design relies on. Surface points in front of the peptide are faded so the far wall of the groove stays readable. Run R1_BoPep4_WT_PEPR1.
BoPEP4_F10_complex-atpep1-ref.jpg: **Figure 10 | AtPep1 (7–23) in PEPR1: the benchmark the protocol was checked on.** The published ligand of this receptor, simulated under the identical protocol as a positive control before any BoPEP4 result was accepted. BoPEP4_T01_md-run-summary.jpg: **Table 1 | Nine molecular dynamics runs, one row each.** Peptide sequence, length, production time, clamp integrity, bidentate Arg487 occupancy, peptide and receptor RMSD, and the acceptance result for every simulation in the set. All runs are 30 ns of production, 1,500 frames at 20 ps, on an NVIDIA A100, at roughly 250 ns per day. Clamp integrity here is the strict measure; the gate column uses a more tolerant clamp criterion and reads higher, which is why the two are kept in separate tables.
BoPEP4_G09_tandem-repeat-sweep.jpg: **Figure 23 | Tandem repeat sweep, one to eight copies, both receptors.** Docking score, buried surface area, buried area per residue, salt-bridge and hydrogen-bond counts, and the number of copies actually engaging the receptor, for constructs carrying one to eight tandem copies of the core. Buried area per residue falls steadily with copy number, from 127 Å² at one copy to 32 Å² at eight, and no construct engages more than three copies however many it carries. Added copies are not engaged, so a tandem construct buys no additional interface.
BoPEP4_G04_clamp-occupancy-all-runs.jpg: **Figure 18 | The C-terminal clamp across the eight peptide-bearing runs.** Two measures of the same anchor for every construct simulated: clamp integrity (green), the strict measure used throughout the Protein Design pages, and the bidentate Arg487 salt bridge beneath it, resolved to atoms (amber). The dashed line is the project's 60% acceptance floor. The two measures agree everywhere except on the His₆-tagged construct, where clamp integrity reads 99.7% and the atom-resolved salt bridge reads 2.4%. A third, more tolerant clamp measure is used by the acceptance gate itself and is reported separately in Table 5.
BoPEP4_F01_complex-wt-ribbon.jpg: **Figure 1 | BoPEP4 (1–23) bound in the PEPR1 leucine-rich-repeat groove.** The modelled complex of full-length BoPEP4 (orange, all atoms) against the 710-residue *Arabidopsis thaliana* PEPR1 ectodomain (green, Cα trace), taken from the first frame of a 30 ns all-atom molecular dynamics run in explicit solvent. BoPEP4_G01_rmsd-trace-wt.jpg: **Figure 15 | Both chains settle inside the acceptance window.** Backbone RMSD from the starting structure over 30 ns for the receptor Cα atoms (green) and the peptide backbone (orange), 1,500 frames at 20 ps. Dashed lines mark the acceptance thresholds set before the run: 3.0 Å for the receptor, 4.0 Å for the peptide. BoPEP4_F05_complex-923-ribbon.jpg: **Figure 5 | BoPEP4 (9–23), the ordered construct, in the same groove.** The manufacturing candidate, fifteen residues against the wild type's twenty-three, modelled and simulated on the identical protocol. BoPEP4_G05_truncation-cliff-haddock.jpg: **Figure 19 | Where the interface stops tolerating an N-terminal cut.** HADDOCK 2.5 water-refined score for seventeen successive N-terminal truncations of BoPEP4, each re-docked on the identical protocol, against PEPR1 (green) and PEPR2 (slate). BoPEP4_G03_per-residue-wt.jpg: **Figure 17 | Contact occupancy and fluctuation, residue by residue.** For each of the 23 residues of wild-type BoPEP4: bars give the share of frames within 4 Å of the receptor, coloured by occupancy band, and the line gives Cα fluctuation (RMSF). Note that this is a 4 Å proximity measure over a trajectory, which is not the same as the buried-surface measure used in the docking interface map, where residues 1 to 6 bury no area at all. BoPEP4_G12_receptor-rmsd-nine-runs.jpg: **Figure 26 | Receptor Cα RMSD across all nine runs, with the apo run as the floor.** Mean receptor backbone RMSD for every simulation in the set, including the receptor simulated with no peptide at all. The apo run is the steadiest trajectory, one hundredth of an ångström below the steadiest bound run, while the bound runs spread over 0.59 Å among themselves. Changing the peptide moves the receptor more than removing it, so no receptor-side difference in this set is read as peptide-induced stabilisation.
